methods.label: Use the domain to bound the sum
methods.explanation:
The radical \(\sqrt{x-1}\) requires \(x\ge1\). This also ensures that \(5x-1\ge4\), so throughout the real domain,
\[
\sqrt{5x-1}\ge2,\qquad \sqrt{x-1}\ge0.
\]
At \(x=1\), the original equation becomes
\[
\sqrt4+\sqrt0=2,
\]
so \(1\) is a solution. If \(x>1\), then \(5x-1>4\), making the first radical greater than \(2\); adding the nonnegative second radical cannot give \(2\).

Therefore the unique solution is \(\boxed{x=1}\), choice D.
methods.levelReason: The domain and elementary square-root comparisons establish uniqueness without any equation-squaring procedure.
